root_cause.text: In the qcom camss VFE interrupt handler, `vfe_isr()` used the 7-entry `MSM_VFE_IMAGE_MASTERS_NUM` loop to call `vfe_isr_reg_update()`, which indexes the 4-entry `vfe->line[]` array, causing out-of-bounds access for line IDs 4–6.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description says `vfe->line[]` is `struct vfe_line line[VFE_LINE_NUM_MAX]` with `VFE_LINE_NUM_MAX(4)`, while `vfe_isr()` iterated to `MSM_VFE_IMAGE_MASTERS_NUM(7)` and passed that index into `vfe_isr_reg_update()`. The patch fixes this by splitting the loops and limiting the `vfe_isr_reg_update()` iteration to `MAX_VFE_OUTPUT_LINES` instead of all write masters.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix VFE ISR handling to iterate over all output lines when processing RDI RUP interrupts.
intent_record.what: The ISR loop that handles `BUS_IRQ_MASK_0_RDI_RUP` interrupts was moved to a separate loop and its upper bound changed from `MSM_VFE_IMAGE_MASTERS_NUM` to `MAX_VFE_OUTPUT_LINES`. The existing loop that handles `BUS_IRQ_MASK_0_COMP_DONE` interrupts remains, but is now placed after the new loop.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the interrupt handler now iterates over the full set of VFE output lines when checking for RDI RUP status bits, instead of limiting that check to the number of image masters. This allows update interrupts for all output lines to be serviced correctly, preventing missed register-update handling for lines beyond `MSM_VFE_IMAGE_MASTERS_NUM`.

grouping_result.intent: Fix VFE ISR handling to iterate over all output lines when processing RDI RUP interrupts.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly targets the VFE ISR interrupt handling loop and fixes iteration over output lines for RDI RUP interrupts, which matches the root cause of an out-of-bounds access caused by using too many master IDs to index the smaller vfe->line[] array.

candidates.rationale: This loop iterates over 7 image masters, but vfe_isr_reg_update() indexes the 4-entry vfe->line[] array using i. Values 4-6 drive the out-of-bounds access described in the root cause.
This call passes the loop index directly into vfe_isr_reg_update(), which uses that value to index vfe->line[]. When i reaches 4-6, it triggers the out-of-bounds access.
